speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our evaluation, how long have you had these symptoms and have there been any recent changes in your diet or travel?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The relief of cramping with bowel movements, urgency, mucus, and the sense of incomplete evacuation are classic signs of inflammation in the rectum and sigmoid colon. Given your history of camping and a sick contact, could you tell me if you have experienced any episodes of visible blood in your stool or unexplained weight loss?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Colitis (likely Campylobacter or Shigella) secondary to contaminated camping water.
